title: Notation
body_md: Given functions $u$ and $v$, $u(x) = \mathcal{O}(v(x))$ implies $u(x) \le c_1 v(x)$ for some $c_1>0$, and $u(x) = \Omega(v(x))$ implies $u(x) \ge c_2 v(x)$ for some $c_2>0$. The notations $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}$ and $\tilde{\Omega}$ hide logarithmic factors in $\mathcal{O}$ and $\Omega$, respectively. Let $\mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma)$ denote the Gaussian distribution with mean $\mu$ and covariance $\Sigma$. For a matrix $A$, let $\|A\|_F$ denote its Frobenius norm and $\|A\|_2$ denote its spectral norm. $I_n$ denotes the $n \times n$ identity matrix  and $\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits(\cdot)$ denotes the column space of a matrix.

body_md: Our formulation accommodates a broader class of control input distributions beyond standard Gaussian signals. Following \citet{kim2026sharp}, the requirements on the input vectors can be relaxed to satisfy only sub-Gaussianity along with an expected persistence of excitation condition. Consequently, the control inputs need not be strictly Gaussian, making the proposed defense framework applicable to a wider range of practical excitation signals.

label: minnormbound
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{minnormbound}
Suppose that Assumptions \ref{as:fullcolumn1} and \ref{as:fullcolumn} hold. 
Then, the  minimum spectral-norm solution satisfying $$H^*\cdot [CE~ CAE ~ \dots ~ CA^{s-1}E] = [I_e ~0~\dots ~0]$$ 
satisfies the geometric bound
\[
\|H^*\|_2 \le \frac{1}{\sigma_{\min}(CE) \sin(\theta)},
\relax\ifmmode \egroup $\hfil \egroup
  \end{trivlist}                                                 
  \else \@badmath \fi
where $\sigma_{\min}(CE) > 0$ is the smallest singular value of $CE$, and $\theta \in (0, \pi/2]$ is the minimal principal angle between  $\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits(CE)$ and  $\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits([CAE ~ \dots ~ CA^{s-1}E])$.

title: Remark
body_md: Equation \eqref{eq:relative_error_bound} provides a principled metric for identifying attacked time steps. Given a solution $(\hat H, \hat J)$, evaluating the filter residual $\hat H y_t - \hat J \mathbf{U}_t^{(k)}$ recovers the residual term $\hat K \mathbf{U}_t^{(k)} + \hat H v_t^{(s)} + \hat H \alpha_t^{(s)} + \hat H \beta_t$. Since the normalized terms $\frac{\hat K \mathbf{U}_t^{(k)}}{\|\hat H\|_2}$, $\alpha_t^{(s)}$, and $\beta_t$ are bounded and small, unattacked periods yield small filter residuals. In contrast, during attacked periods, large magnitude of adversarial attacks $v_t^{(s)}$ induce large residual spikes under clear separation between normal and corrupted data, enabling attack detection.

title: Proof
body_md:
For  simplicity, let $L := [CAE ~ \dots ~ CA^{s-1}E]$. 

$(\Longrightarrow)$ Suppose such a matrix $H \in \mathbb{R}^{e \times r}$ exists. 
First, $H CE = I_e$ implies $e = \mathop{\mathrm{rank}}\nolimits(I_e) = \mathop{\mathrm{rank}}\nolimits(H CE) \le \mathop{\mathrm{rank}}\nolimits(CE) \le e$, so $\mathop{\mathrm{rank}}\nolimits(CE) = e$.
Second, let $y \in \mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits(CE) \cap \mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits(L )$. Then $y = CE u = L  v$ for some $u \in \mathbb{R}^e$ and $v \in \mathbb{R}^{e(s-1)}$. Multiplying by $H$ yields:
\[
u = I_e u = H CE u = H y = H L  v = 0 \cdot v = 0.
\relax\ifmmode \egroup $\hfil \egroup
  \end{trivlist}                                                 
  \else \@badmath \fi
Thus $y =  0$, proving $\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits(CE) \cap \mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits(L ) = \{0\}$.

\medskip
$(\Longleftarrow)$ Suppose $\mathop{\mathrm{rank}}\nolimits(CE) = e$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits(CE) \cap \mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits(L) = \{0\}$. 
Let $V = \{x+y\in\mathbb{R}^r: x\in\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits(CE), y\in \mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits(L) \}$. Any vector $z \in V$ can be expressed as $z = CE u + L v$. If 
\[
CE u_1 + L v_1 = CE u_2 + L v_2,
\relax\ifmmode \egroup $\hfil \egroup
  \end{trivlist}                                                 
  \else \@badmath \fi
then $CE(u_1 - u_2) = L (v_2 - v_1) \in \mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits(CE) \cap \mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits(L) = \{0\}$. Hence $CE(u_1 - u_2) = 0$, and since $\mathop{\mathrm{rank}}\nolimits(CE) = e$, it follows that $u_1 = u_2$.

Therefore, the linear map $H_0 : V \to \mathbb{R}^e$ given by
\[
H_0(CE u + L v) = u
\relax\ifmmode \egroup $\hfil \egroup
  \end{trivlist}                                                 
  \else \@badmath \fi
is well-defined because $u$ is uniquely determined for every $z \in V$. Evaluation at $v = 0$ and $u = 0$ respectively gives $H_0 CE = I_e$ and $H_0 L = 0$.

Finally, extend $H_0$ to all of $\mathbb{R}^r$ by choosing a complementary subspace $W$ such that $\mathbb{R}^r = V + W$ with $V \cap W = \{0\}$, and setting $H(w) = 0$ for all $w \in W$. This yields the desired matrix $H\in\mathbb{R}^{e\times r}$.

body_md:
For simplicity, let $L = \begin{bmatrix} CAE & \dots & CA^{s-1}E \end{bmatrix}$. Also, let $P_L^\perp = I_r - L L^+$, where $L^+$ is the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse of $L$. The constraint $H^* L = 0$ parameterizes $H^* = X P_L^\perp$, which reduces $H^* CE = I_e$ to $X (P_L^\perp CE) = I_e$. Under Assumptions~\ref{as:fullcolumn1} and~\ref{as:fullcolumn}, $P_L^\perp CE$ has full column rank $e$, yielding the unique minimum spectral-norm solution $H^* = (P_L^\perp CE)^+$ with $\|H^*\|_2 = \frac{1}{\sigma_{\min}(P_L^\perp CE)}$.

For any unit vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^e$, let $y = CE x \in \mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits(CE)$. By the definitions of singular values and the minimal principal angle $\theta$:
\[
\|P_L^\perp CE x\|_2 = \|P_L^\perp y\|_2 \ge \sin(\theta) \|y\|_2 \ge \sin(\theta) \sigma_{\min}(CE).
\relax\ifmmode \egroup $\hfil \egroup
  \end{trivlist}                                                 
  \else \@badmath \fi
Taking the infimum over $\|x\|_2 = 1$ yields $\sigma_{\min}(P_L^\perp CE) \ge \sigma_{\min}(CE) \sin(\theta) > 0$. Taking the reciprocal completes the proof.
